sections.heading: How to Play Guardian
sections.body:
[h2 type=bar toc="How to Play Guardian"][color=c11]Guardian Druid Rotation in Midnight Season 2[/color][/h2]
The Guardian Rotation is one of the most simple and easy to manage in the whole game.
We have only a few short cooldown spells we want to use as often as possible and no real debuffs or procs to track.
The main thing to focus on for Guardian is ensuring you have enough rage to use defensively when you require it.



[wrapper width=1100px][box border=true]
[center][table style=grid]
[tr][td]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=spell_misc_emotionangry size=medium type=round color=c11 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=c11]Avoid Rage Waste:[/color][/b] Rage should be spent intentionally. Unecessary over-use of Ironfur will be a huge DPS loss.
	[/td][/tr]
[/table]
[hr]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=spell_druid_thrash size=medium type=round color=c11 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=c11]Keep Abilities on Cooldown:[/color][/b] Making sure you are casting Mangle and Thrash as often as possible ensures the rotation flows smoothly. 
	[/td][/tr]
[/table]
[hr]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=spell_nature_stoneclawtotem size=medium type=round color=c11 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=c11]Rotate Defensive Cooldowns:[/color][/b] Having a defensive cooldown at the right time makes a world of difference as a tank spec.[/td]
	[/tr]
[/table]
[/td][/tr][/table]
[/center]
[/box][/wrapper]
[pad]

sections.heading: Rotation Priority

[h2 type=bar toc="Rotation Priority"][icon name=ability_racial_bearform type=round size=medium inline=true color=c11][/icon] Best Guardian Druid Rotation[/h2]

sections.heading: Major Cooldowns
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Major Cooldowns" type=bar][icon name=Spell_druid_incarnation color=c11 inline=true size=medium type=round][/icon] Guardian Druid Major Cooldown Usage[/h2]
Guardian Druid has a small selection of cooldowns with varying durations and timers. In ideal circumstances, such as when you have a full understanding of the encounter, you should be able to time or hold certain cooldowns to pair with others as they become available again. Do this only if you won't lose any cooldown uses during the encounter. If you don't understand how to time your cooldowns properly, then use them off cooldown when available.
[pad]
[tabs name="cds" uniform=true iconborders=true]
[tab name="Berserk / Incarnation" icon=Spell_druid_incarnation ]
While this buff is active, you want to try to get as many casts of [spell=77758] and [spell=33917] off as possible, while also spending your Rage on [spell=6807], [spell=400254], or [spell=192081] to avoid capping Rage. 
[/tab]

[tab name="Lunar Beam" icon=Spell_nature_moonglow]
You should aim to use as many [spell=6807][color=q]s[/color]/[spell=400254][color=q]s[/color] as possible during the buff window, as it is a large damage boost. It also grants us a considerable health boost and can be one of our better defensive cooldowns.

[/tab]
[tab name="Heart of the Wild" icon=Spell_holy_blessingofagility]
Pressing [spell=1261867] casts a single spell depending on which form you are in.
For Cat Form this is [spell=274837] - A large single target DoT.
For Human/No Form it casts [spell=48438] - A short HoT for you and your group.
For Boomkin Form it casts [spell=191037] - A buff that lasts 8 seconds that deals low damage to all targets in combat with you slowly.
Generally it is used in Cat Form for the large single target DPS increase but sometimes the group heal can save lives.

[/tab]
[tab name="Survival Instincts" icon=Ability_druid_tigersroar]
A 50% damage reduction on a fairly long cooldown. This is our biggest damage reduction cooldown and should be used sparingly for dangerous periods during a pull or encounter.

[/tab]
[tab name="Barkskin" icon=Spell_nature_stoneclawtotem]
An extremely short cooldown that should be used as frequently as possible to smooth overall damage intake. Rarely, you can hold it for a short time to align with bigger damage spikes.

[/tab]
[/tabs]

sections.heading: Advanced Tips
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Advanced Tips" type=bar][color=c11][icon name=Inv_artifact_tome01 type=round size=medium inline=true color=c11][/icon] Guardian Druid Advanced Tips[/color][/h2]

[pad]
[tabs name="advanced" uniform=true iconborders=true]
[tab name="Spending Rage" icon=ability_druid_ironfur]
	[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c11] Spending Rage [/color][/h3]
Whether you want to improve surviving or want to improve your damage. Spending rage will be the main focal point of both.
Pressing [spell=192081] when you don't actually need it defensively is now quite a significant dps loss.
As our goal is to stay above 80 rage with each cast of [spell=6807] due to [spell=1253035], pressing Ironfur drains that rage quickly and stops the cycle of high rage expenditure.
This means we end up filling our GCD's with useless abilities like [spell=213764] which generate no rage and deal very little damage. The more you are swiping the less DPS you are doing efficiently.
Alternatively, not pressing Ironfur when a large physical hit is coming or significant flow of melee swings, can easily lead to death. So finding a comfortable balance between these 2 is integral.
[/tab]
[/tabs]
[pad]
